difficultyRationale: Tests the special treatment of exception parameters in a multi-catch clause.
prompt: Inside `catch (IOException | SQLException ex)`, which statement about assigning a new value to `ex` is correct?
explanation: An exception parameter in a multi-catch clause is implicitly final. Assigning another value to that parameter is a compile-time error.

options.text: Reassignment is allowed because catch parameters are ordinary local variables.
options.explanation: Multi-catch parameters have the special rule that they are implicitly final.

options.text: Reassignment is a compile-time error because the multi-catch parameter is implicitly final.
options.explanation: That restriction is part of the multi-catch language rules.

options.text: Reassignment is allowed only to another IOException.
options.explanation: The issue is finality, not which alternative type the replacement value belongs to.

options.text: Reassignment is allowed only when the catch body rethrows ex.
options.explanation: Rethrowing does not change the implicit-final rule.
